guarantees.claim: When no error source asserts its valid signal, hw2reg.err_code.d is driven to all zeros.

The always_comb block implements a priority encoder: hw2reg.err_code.d equals the {code, info} of the highest priority error source with a valid flag, with priority order app_err > errchecker_err > sha3_err > entropy_err > msgfifo_err.

formal.consequent: hw2reg.err_code.d == (app_err.valid ? {app_err.code, app_err.info} : (errchecker_err.valid ? {errchecker_err.code, errchecker_err.info} : (sha3_err.valid ? {sha3_err.code, sha3_err.info} : (entropy_err.valid ? {entropy_err.code, entropy_err.info} : (msgfifo_err.valid ? {msgfifo_err.code, msgfifo_err.info} : '0)))))

uncertain_points.claim: When no error valid is asserted, hw2reg.err_code.d is set to '0. It is unclear whether '0 is a legal error code value or carries special meaning (e.g., 'no error'). The intended error reporting behavior may require retention of the last error or a separate valid flag.
uncertain_points.risk: Software may misinterpret a zero code as 'no error' when a transient error occurred but was not latched, or may use zero as a normal operational indicator, causing a false positive or missed fault.

uncertain_points.claim: If a high-priority error and a low-priority error occur simultaneously, only the high-priority error is captured. The lower-priority error information (code+info) is overwritten and lost.
uncertain_points.cond: Multiple error valid signals asserted in the same cycle
uncertain_points.risk: A lower-priority security‑critical error (e.g., sha3 integrity failure) could be masked by a higher-priority non‑security error, preventing software from reacting to the integrity violation.

formal_sketch.antecedent: Multiple error valid signals asserted in the same cycle
formal_sketch.consequent: only the high-priority error is captured. The lower-priority error information (code+info) is overwritten and lost

security_implications: The error code register hw2reg.err_code.d aggregates error indications from multiple sources, some of which may relate to security (sha3 integrity, entropy errors, errchecker). The priority encoding can silently drop lower-priority errors, potentially suppressing evidence of a security violation (e.g., a SHA3 fault) if a higher-priority non‑security error is active concurrently. Additionally, clearing the register to zero when no error is active may erase transient evidence of a security event before software can read it, hindering forensic analysis.
